events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
Safety screen. The rider's complaint states the driver was "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that she "was scared and felt unsafe" — a dangerous-driving allegation squarely within SAFE-2 [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Separately, the driver's own written statement calls the rider "stupid" [F6], which is an insult aimed at the other party in the trip record and is at least a suspected case of "abuse of any kind" under SAFE-1 [F6][SAFE-1]. On both branches I do not rule on the merits: the trace confirms the safety screen passes and the only allowed outcome is escalate [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

What the human reviewer must check. The contemporaneous records cover only efficiency, not driving manner: actual 10.5 km vs optimal 10.6 km (-0.1 km) and 15.9 min vs estimated 16.5 min (-0.6 min) [F1][F2]. A slightly shorter, slightly faster trip is equally consistent with brisk-but-safe driving and with the described speeding-plus-hard-braking-but-shoulder-overtaking, so it neither corroborates nor refutes the account [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. There is no speed, braking, lane-use or telematics fact in the table, and no traffic incident fact, so the allegation cannot be tested against route data [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], but its content is pick-up logistics only (rider outside University Hall in a blue shirt; driver ~6 min away in a blue Prius) [F3][F4]; its silence on driving does not discredit a passenger who had no reason to narrate driving in a logistics thread [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2]. The driver's denial in F6 ("I drove normally") is a statement made after the trip, and the same statement contains the insult, which the reviewer should weigh in reading it [F6][SAFE-1]. The parties' profiles — rider 4.8 rating, 0 disputes/90 d [F7]; driver 4.78 rating, 705 trips/90 d, 0 disputes/90 d [F8] — are context only and decide nothing here [F7][F8][SAFE-2].

Remedy note. Because this is a safety escalation and no fare or gps detour fact is in dispute, no amount can be computed from a fare record; any monetary remedy is for the human reviewer [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Escalation asks for a person, not for a determination, so neither a fare ruling nor an account flag is issued at this stage [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human reviewer: summarise the first-hand dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) and the driver's post-trip insult, note the 995 / driver commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths, and have the reviewer read F6 in context to decide whether SAFE-1 abuse and/or SAFE-2 apply before any fare decision.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen. The rider's complaint states the driver was "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that she "was scared and felt unsafe" — a dangerous-driving allegation squarely within SAFE-2 [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Separately, the driver's own written statement calls the rider "stupid" [F6], which is an insult aimed at the other party in the trip record and is at least a suspected case of "abuse of any kind" under SAFE-1 [F6][SAFE-1]. On both branches I do not rule on the merits: the trace confirms the safety screen passes and the only allowed outcome is escalate [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

What the human reviewer must check. The contemporaneous records cover only efficiency, not driving manner: actual 10.5 km vs optimal 10.6 km (-0.1 km) and 15.9 min vs estimated 16.5 min (-0.6 min) [F1][F2]. A slightly shorter, slightly faster trip is equally consistent with brisk-but-safe driving and with the described speeding-plus-hard-braking-but-shoulder-overtaking, so it neither corroborates nor refutes the account [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. There is no speed, braking, lane-use or telematics fact in the table, and no traffic incident fact, so the allegation cannot be tested against route data [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], but its content is pick-up logistics only (rider outside University Hall in a blue shirt; driver ~6 min away in a blue Prius) [F3][F4]; its silence on driving does not discredit a passenger who had no reason to narrate driving in a logistics thread [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2]. The driver's denial in F6 ("I drove normally") is a statement made after the trip, and the same statement contains the insult, which the reviewer should weigh in reading it [F6][SAFE-1]. The parties' profiles — rider 4.8 rating, 0 disputes/90 d [F7]; driver 4.78 rating, 705 trips/90 d, 0 disputes/90 d [F8] — are context only and decide nothing here [F7][F8][SAFE-2].

Remedy note. Because this is a safety escalation and no fare or gps detour fact is in dispute, no amount can be computed from a fare record; any monetary remedy is for the human reviewer [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. Escalation asks for a person, not for a determination, so neither a fare ruling nor an account flag is issued at this stage [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The system-records-override rule applies to a gps/timeline/fare record on the same point; here the records cover only distance and duration [F1][F2] and say nothing about speed, braking or lane use, so the complete timestamped chat [F3][F4][F5] cannot displace the rider's first-hand account of how the car was driven [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2].

The driver's clean 90-day history (3.9 y, 4.78, 705 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) [F8] is context only and cannot answer a specific first-hand dangerous-driving report from this trip; profile facts never decide the case and do not bar a human review [F8][SAFE-2].

The rider's profile [F7] does not support the driver either: 0 disputes in 90 days is equally consistent with a credible first report and is not evidence about the driving manner; profile facts do not decide the safety question [F7][SAFE-2].

Correctly identified that the driver's F6 remark is an insult, but whether it is abuse under SAFE-1 is a reading of the words for the human reviewer, not a finding I may make; the case escalates rather than being decided on it [F6][SAFE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation: she states the driver was speeding and braking hard the whole way and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was scared and felt unsafe; the case record itself is filed as a safety dispute, so this is not a mere fare or route argument.
The driver's own written statement calls the rider 'stupid', which is an insult directed at the passenger in the trip record and reads as verbal abuse/harassment of a rider by the driver.

Because the file contains a dangerous-driving allegation of the kind SAFE-2 covers and abuse of the kind SAFE-1 covers, the correct disposition is not an automatic fare ruling: the case must go to a person for review, with the facts summarised for the human reviewer.

The system records neither an off-route segment nor excess distance (actual 10.5 km vs optimal 10.6 km, -0.1 km) and no traffic/weather facts exist, so the safety allegation cannot be tested against route data and must be assessed from the rider's account and the driver's statement — which supports escalation, not a finding for the driver.

The rider is a 4.0-year account holder with rating 4.8 and 0 disputes in 90 days, so her safety report is not the pattern of a habitual or vexatious complainant; the escalation should be handled as a genuine safety report about an established driver with 705 trips in 90 days.

weaknesses: There is no telematics evidence of speeding or harsh braking: F1 and F2 show only a slightly shorter-than-optimal, slightly faster-than-estimated trip (10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal; 15.9 vs 16.5 min), which the driver will use to argue the driving was normal.

The chat record (F3, F4, F5) contains no message in which the rider complains about the driving or asks the driver to slow down during the trip, which the other side will use to argue the safety account is uncorroborated.

The driver's 'stupid' remark in F6 is a post-trip written insult rather than an in-trip threat or intimidation, so the judge may treat it as rudeness within SAFE-1 rather than a clear-cut safety escalation.
The driver profile (F8) shows a long-standing account with 0 disputes upheld in 90 days, which supports the driver's denial in F6 that anything was wrong.
Because this is a safety case, the rider's file contains no fare facts, so no refund amount can be computed from a fare fact; any monetary remedy would have to come from the human reviewer.

claims.assertion: This is a dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder) made by the rider in the complaint, so under SAFE-2 the case must go to a person and no automated ruling on the fare should be issued; the mandated summary should note the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths.

The rider's written complaint is a safety allegation with no corroborating system record: the GPS track shows the trip finished in 15.9 min against a 16.5 min estimate and 10.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route, i.e. slightly faster and slightly shorter, with no recorded deviation or excessive-distance finding (F1, F2).

The rider's fear and the allegation are unsupported by the only contemporaneous records available: the chat contains nothing about driving (F3, F4), the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F5), and no traffic or weather incident facts exist for this trip — so the rider's statement stands alone against the system records, which win.

The driver's own written statement — 'The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally.' (F6) — contains a personal insult directed at the rider, which is the kind of abuse language SAFE-1 makes a human-review matter; I flag it rather than rely on it, and it is submitted content that cannot outweigh the complete, timestamped chat record (F5).

The driver has a clean record that argues against any account action: 3.9 years on the platform, rating 4.78, 705 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F8) — profile facts are offered only against any flag_account request, not as the finding itself.

The rider's own profile shows no history of disputed trips (4.0 years, rating 4.8, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, F7), so the single complaint is not supported by any pattern of conduct on either side.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a specific, first-hand dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) and no clause lets me disprove it: GPS gives only distance and duration (F1, F2), so a passenger who felt unsafe at legal-but-brisk driving cannot be contradicted by any fact in the table, and the matter must go to a person under SAFE-2.

The driver's post-trip statement calls the rider 'stupid' (F6). The other side will read that as exactly the kind of personal attack SAFE-1 is directed at, and it invites human review of the driver's conduct and possible account action — it also weakens the credibility of the very statement in which the driver says 'I drove normally.'

Nothing in the record speaks to driving manner at all: there is no speed, harsh-braking or telematics fact, and my only support is an absence of evidence (no traffic/weather facts returned, F1, F2), which the rider will call an absence of proof rather than proof of safe driving.

points.response: Agreed on the disposition: the rider's speeding / hard-braking / shoulder-overtaking complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 sends the file to a person with no automated fare ruling — which is exactly what my brief asks for (F6; SAFE-2).

The distance and duration facts (10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal; 15.9 min vs 16.5 min, F1, F2) are an efficiency measure, not a driving-manner measure: they can be fully consistent with speeding with hard braking offset by the shoulder overtaking, so they neither disprove nor corroborate the allegation and the file still goes to a human (F1, F2; SAFE-2).

The 'system records win' rule governs contradiction of a statement by a gps/timeline/fare record on the same point; there is no speed, braking or lane-use record at all in this file (F1, F2), so a complete timestamped chat (F3, F4, F5) cannot displace the rider's first-hand account of how the car was driven — she had no reason to describe driving in a pick-up logistics chat.

I note the driver's concession that F6 contains a personal insult directed at the rider; that language is abuse in the trip record and reinforces rather than defuses the SAFE-1 human-review route, and it is not softened by the fact that the chat record is complete (F6, F5; SAFE-1).

The driver's clean 90-day history (3.9 y, 4.78 rating, 705 trips, 0 disputes, F8) does not answer a specific first-hand dangerous-driving report from a passenger on that trip, since the record shows no ride in which any passenger has previously had to report driving at all (F8; SAFE-2).

The rider's profile (4.0 y, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes, F7) cuts my way, not the driver's: a long-standing rider with no dispute history has no incentive to file a safety report, so the single complaint is credible on its face and belongs with a human reviewer (F7; SAFE-1).

I do not contest that a dangerous-driving allegation is on the file — I said the same in my D1 and requested escalate under SAFE-2; but the allegation is only the rider's untested account and is contradicted by the trip's own records, which show 10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal and 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated (F1, F2).

I do not defend the 'stupid' remark in F6; it is the driver's post-trip written statement, not an in-trip message, and SAFE-1 leaves the question whether it is abuse to the human reviewer reading the text — which is why the case must go to a person rather than be decided against the fare.

Agreed on disposition: the file contains both a dangerous-driving allegation (SAFE-2) and a possible abuse remark (SAFE-1), so no automated finding is made and escalation is the correct action, exactly as my D1 requested.

The absence of route corroboration cuts both ways: F1 and F2 show a trip that was slightly shorter and slightly faster than optimal with no excess distance, and no traffic/weather facts were returned, so there is no system record of the erratic driving the rider describes — the rider's account therefore rests on her statement alone, which SAFE-2 sends to a person, not to a finding for her.

The rider's clean profile (4.0 years, 4.8, 0 disputes in 90 days, F7) shows only that she is not a habitual complainant; the driver's equally clean record (3.9 years, 4.78, 705 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, F8) shows the same on the other side, and under SAFE-2 neither profile decides the safety question — the human reviewer does.
